utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Bolton, may I remind you of the affirmation that you had at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Bolton.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will simply start with a matter of clarification which was drawn to my attention again kindly by the registry yesterday. We tendered a document which was taken from Rule 65 ter 230 of the Prosecution proposed lift of exhibits. We would simple wish to make it clear that's the only document which we sought to tender yesterday were the first three pages which we used in evidence, and for the record, I will give the ERN number which is N001-5304, N001-5306.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And with the assistance of the usher, I will give Mr. Bolton his binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bolton, I'll kindly ask you to go back once again to the document under tab number 2 of your binder and that is the special report of the 16 of August, to the first page, please. And I'd like to draw your attention to the third paragraph of that document. You remember yesterday you gave evidence that in your view, the clothe or clothing worn by the deceased were of the a civilian nature. Can you remember telling me that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I draw your attention to the third paragraph of that report, second sentence it says this: "All of the deceased were dressed in civilian clothes." So that would be consistent your evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this: "All of the deceased were unarmed at the time the mission observed them. Although it must be noted that from the conditions of the bodies that more than one day had passed since these men had died. Some bodies had been rolled over or moved slightly," and again that would be consistent your evidence is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then a report goes on to sound a bit of a cautionary note. It says this: "The possibility that one or more of these person had been carrying arms at the time of death cannot be excluded at this time." Is that correct? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that at this stage, you could not exclude that possibility, sir?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nor was there any indication that they were armed either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if evidence was given in this court that two automatic weapons and a submachine-gun Thomson with matching ammunition was found in the general areas where the bodies were found, you would consider that to be relevant, I suppose, to whether or not those people had, in fact, been carrying weapons at the time, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct. However, around those bodies or in the vicinity I did not observe any spent ammunition that would indicate the type of weapon, specifically the named weapon that you just mentioned, the Thomson.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You're not excluding, sir, that at that time there may have been such ammunition used or not used, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw no indication of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, if a witness were to give evidence in this courtroom that he or she saw gun-fire coming from the house or the group of houses where those three men had been staying until that time, again you would agree that this could be relevant to the issue as to whether or not those people might have been carrying arms at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know which houses you're referring to. However, if they are houses that I entered, there was no indication of any firing from those houses when I entered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you will recall that of the group of the four houses that had received quite a great deal of fire, one of those houses had, I think you described it as burned down, is that correct, or in part?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again without being specific about which house -- a number of houses had sustained damage. Then I can't-- I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm talk of a group of four houses which were in the general area are you located the three bodies. Can you recall those four houses?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about white houses on the right-hand side of the road at the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in that general area, do you recall seeing one of the houses which was still smouldering or which had been burned.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say there were a number of houses that had sustained that type of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you enter any of the house that had burned down?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The houses that I entered had no indication within them that there had been any firing from within them. In other words, there were no spent casings remaining there at the time that I entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said you entered two or three houses; is that correct? That's what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I entered three possibly four houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did not enter any of the houses that hadn't been burned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a house shown on a photograph yesterday, a photograph that I had taken, showing the location of three -- three bodies. You will recall I annotated that -- I had annotated that photograph showing the locations. I did not enter the building on the left-hand side of that photograph which was damaged by fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other buildings I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. You will remember, sir, that yesterday a number of issues were raised about the report of this 16th of August about the procedure in which it's being prepared and the way in which it was processed within the organisation; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said that you believed that Ms. Eileen Simpson might have been the author of that document, but I think you indicated that you were not certain about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have direct knowledge of that being the case, but I cannot envisage anyone else being the author of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that Ms. Simpson is a lawyer by profession?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe she is legally qualified, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you know at the time that she had been trial attorney in the US?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We've been warned twice now. Well, at least I have been warned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Three strikes and you're out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll take that very seriously Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, at that time that Ms. Simpson had spent two years prior to your arrival in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew she was there prior to my arrival, I couldn't tell you for how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware, sir, from your experience with the OSCE that HDO - that's human dimension officers - were generally lawyers; is that correct? That's the general practice in the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself am not a lawyer, yet I was a human dimension officer in Kosovo and that is not -- often they have some form of legal training; that is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But I think you've indicated that Ms. Simpson, as far as you could tell, had no military background; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that one of the main responsibility of a HDO, a human dimension officer, is to monitor and report about particular event or incidents? Is that one of the main functions and role of the HDOs?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in that particular cases in Skopje, in that particular field operation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is one of their responsibilities as well to keep contact with the local authorities and international organisations which may be in the area?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again that is not always the case, but in the case of the Skopje field operation, I believe yes it was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I think briefly, the procedure pursuant to which such a special report is being prepared. And if I understood you properly, the person would prepare the report and the report would then be passed on to his or her superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. At the time she reported normally to the head of mission. However, the deputy head of mission was also very much involved in these issues in Skopje at the time, and she -- I can envisage that she may have passed the report to either of those. There were occasions - and I do not know that it was the case on this occasion - when reports could potentially be bypass or could bypass that chain and could go directly to the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case you wouldn't be surprised at all if the report had indeed gone to the deputy head of the mission? That would be the normal procedure, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be the responsible of the deputy head to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the report, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- no, no. The deputy head or the person checking the report would do two things: Check it for grammar and make sure the thing reads correctly and also to ensure that it is appropriate, in other words, that there aren't -- and I'm now talking not so much about human dimension reports but political reports that may be substantive diplomatically, but in this case, the job would to ensure it reads correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: He will also take responsibility for the report, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: To an extent. In field reporting, the reporting officer, in other words, the officer authoring the report takes responsibility for the content of the report. Because they are actually reporting an event or an incident that they have observed. The responsibility for clearing it for dissemination is the responsibility of whoever it may be. In this case I would presume that it would be the deputy head of mission or head of mission, which is normally the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that the report goes out to Vienna and then to the states as the report of the Skopje mission and not as the report of Ms. Simpson? She doesn't even sign the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And by contrast, sir, your report, the report of the 15 is a report that is, as I understand it, for internal use only sent for information in that case to a number of people in the HQ in Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not my decision as to how far it is disseminated. That is a decision for the headquarters, and I inform them. They decide who they are going to inform.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, do you recall yesterday I asked you a number of questions about the presence of the NLA in Ljuboten and I read the following passage to you from again the same report. I will read it out to you. It's the fifth paragraph at page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please read slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will consider that not to be a strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Report from other international observers in the area indicate that they were EAAG in the village in civilian clothes and that there was an exchange of fire from deer rifles within the village." Do you recall me reading that passage to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Sorry, could you direct me to where it is in the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, it is page 3 of the report and it would be the fifth paragraph, last sentence. It starts with the words: "Reports from."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And yesterday you asked me or raised the issue of these international observers and I promised I would come back to it, so I'm going to come back to it now. You would agree, sir, that in addition to the OSCE at the time the UNN was also monitoring the activities in the region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they were also gathering information like you did at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will just ask to go into private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if can I ask the registry to bring up --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask the registry to bring up document 1D140, which is ERN 1D001668.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, it is under tab 40, 4-0, of your binder? Sir, as you can see from this document, it's -- the title suggests it's an EUMM situation report on FYROM, and it's dated 12 August at 16 hours. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may draw your attention to the first document in that paragraph which starts with "general situation." I will read it out to you: "General situation: Macedonian force -- security forces continued massive attack against positions of rebel National Liberation Army, NLA, positions in the Tetovo area and north-east along the road to the Kosovo border. NLA has moved closer to Skopje by gaining control over the village of Ljuboten five kilometres north of Skopje outskirts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it goes on to say this: "The highway between Tetovo and Skopje is closed after reported NLA attack at Bojane, ten kilometers west of Skopje." Just about this incident, sir, would that be the location of the incidents which you witnessed and recalled yesterday?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine that they're referring to the same incident, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I ask I can you to turn to what would the fourth paragraph in the main text which starts with the word "Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "Ljuboten, five kilometre north of Skopje outskirts, an area of mine explosions on 10 August, killing eight soldiers, came under attack by NLA on 12 August." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "And forced by several hundred rebels from Kosovo according to Crisis Management Centre, CMC, information to UNN." Now just pause for a second, sir, did you receive information at the time that a number of reinforcement, perhaps as much as 300 men from Kosovo who were destined for Ljuboten were intercepted somewhere around Radishan? Is that information that you had in your possession?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did have reports on a number of occasions passed to us -- passed to the OSCE and then on to me of people crossing the border from Kosovo. We endeavoured on every occasion to try and verify this, and I certainly cannot say that it did not occur, but I certainly cannot say that we were able to corroborate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "ICRC will try to evacuate civilians and reportedly wounded. Police station in nearby ethnic Macedonian village of Ljubanci is also under NLA attack while security forces are responding. Situation unclear." Sir, did you have that information from the EUMM in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The EUMM and the OSCE would have received that information if it came from the Crisis Management Centre. It would have -- the normal procedure is that it would have gone into joint central, the coordination cell which was -- which fed information to both the EUMM and OSCE monitors. The -- there was a lot of information going around in those days. And the impression that this conveys is not the one that have I from my observations on the ground, and I do not know what the source of this information is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you saying you did not have that information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have that -- I did not have that information. I was reporting information but receiving very little, and I was going requested for information on a continuous basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what you said about the information coming from the CMC, do I understand you properly that this information could have been transmitted to the HQ in Skopje which would be the usual procedure?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If EUMM received it from the CMC I would imagine -- I would expect the IC coordination cell to oversee it also.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it's likely in any case possible that the information was also available to the person who prepared the report on the 16th of August. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, there is another document which I would like -- sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D28, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I think you've indicated yesterday that the ICRC was in or at least close to the village of Ljuboten on the 12th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a question of defining "close." They were some kilometres to the south. I do not recall the name of the precise location at which I know they moved to temporarily before moving away again. But they were some kilometres from the village of Ljuboten, to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if they moved around during that day to other locations?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe they moved any closer to -- or certainly not to my knowledge did they move any closer to Ljuboten than that. They were very concerned about the security situation. The gun-fire and the detonations of those days could be heard for some distance, and they did not want to endanger their people by getting too close. So they were asking us for assessments of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that they might have asked other people as well for information?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I expect they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall as well, and I think that was your evidence yesterday, that they tried to organise a convoy and I think you said they were forced to retreat because of the security situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The -- there was discussion between ICRC, UNHCR, and ourselves as to options and there had been also been requests by telephone from villagers for assistance in organising an evacuation. However, for a variety of reasons, security and others, it was decided that this was not an option that three organisations wished to apply. So there was no attempt to organise or plan an evacuation in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd now like to show you a document that is 1D126 and the ERN number is 1D001636 and that's under tab 19 in your binder. Sir, again this document would appear to be from monitor Skopje to HQ EUMM and is dated the 13th of August, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like you to focus on the last paragraph on that document, if you may, under the heading "security."

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please. And I'll read it out to you. It says this: "Reports of fierce exchanges between ARM, that's the army, and EAAG in the Ljuboten and Ljubanci areas at 1400 hours 12 July - and that would seem to be a typo, 12 August - were confirmed late in the day by ICRC who had attempted to organise a convoy of vehicles to extract Albanian citizens of Ljuboten from the affected area. The ICRC team reported that when they arrive at a spot between a police check-point and an army check-point in the general area DM-385580 they encountered a roadblock manned by armed civilians who were abusive and chased them away from the area." Sir, I suppose you would agree that's the information which the EUMM would have received from the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't believe it to be entirely accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I believe that -- not from EUMM but I believe that may well very close to the location at which I said I knew that ICRC had moved to. That being the case, the intention of ICRC was to establish what the situation was, and they were unable to do so. This was not an attempt to organise a convoy. This was an attempt to assess the situation and in order to gain more information as to whether or not such a plan, such an option, was a possibility or feasible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree, sir, that you don't know where the ICRC would have obtained that information from. You're unable to say anything about this; Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where ICRC had it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, which information?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you've indicated or at least you've agreed with me that they might have received information from sources other than you; is that correct? That's what you said a bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so you are not able to state with any certainty where the ICRC could have obtained that information which in turn they transmitted to the EUMM; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I do not believe that information to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, again, you don't know what the source of that information is?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, sir, that information could have been transmitted to your HQ in Skopje. You don't know whether that is the case or not?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OSCE coordination cell would have, I believe, received probably a copy of this very report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it's also perhaps a report that was in the possession of the person who wrote the report on the 16th of August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D29, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn your attention to the report again under tab 2 at page 2. And simply to read this part of the report on that day. "In addition to the mortar emplacement outside of town, there is an ethnic Albanian armed group presence in town as well." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, again can you direct me to --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. This is the first paragraph. It's not a full paragraph, it comes from the previous page and it starts with the word "in addition." That would be the third line on the top of page 2.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "In addition to the mortar emplacement outside the town, there is an ethnic Albanian armed group presence in town as well." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose you would agree that your colleagues from the OSCE would not have made this finding unless they had evidence to that effect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidence or information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would sum -- it could be either.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you -- you at the time also, sir, you were aware that there were two NLA positions very close to the village of Ljuboten at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, very close is -- is an ill defined phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll define it for you, sir. If we look at the bottom of the same page, the very last paragraph with the word starting, "It is now known." Can you see that? It's the very last line on this page you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "It is now known that there is an EAAG position north of the village 'significant' position located in the area of Ljubotenski" -- it says Racila, and it should be Bacila. And it goes on to say, "Reliable sources indicate that the second position may have been associated with the mine strike on government forces in the area and that Macedonian forces appropriately engaged this EAAG position with mortar fire from below the village." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again you would agree that that's a finding that your colleagues from the HQ would not do without either evidence or information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did have you that information in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have information that the -- that there were possibly NLA -- there was NLA activity in the area of -- the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you now to turn to the last page of this document. And go to the paragraph starting with the word "finally it appears." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says this: "It appears highly likely that there were EAAG, in the village during the recent hostilities and that the EAAG have influence in the village. In this context, the HDO finds reports that ethnic Albanian villagers remained in their homes during the hostilities 'because they are loyal citizens who had no reason to leave,' profoundly disturbing. The mission is unaware of a village free of EAAG influence in which the majority of the ethnic Albanian population made the decision to remain in their homes with their families when an armed conflict was erupting in the village or nearby. It only happens with an EAAG presence." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the report goes to say this in the next paragraph: "There does appear to be an EAAG tactic involving the use of, at the very least, 'suggestions' and informal pressure on villagers to remain during fighting. This tactic effectively results in the use of civilians as human shields. It also leaves them exposed to incidents with troops. It is intended to produce either government inaction in the face of aggression or incidents that can be exploited for propaganda. It is, thus, not only illegal, but the cynical abuse of a friendly, vulnerable local population by armed groups." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, I suppose your colleagues would not make that sort of findings without any evidence to back them up; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Or information. I think you have indicated, sir that in your proofing note, however, you were unaware of any incidents of human shield or the NLA having recourse to human shield in Macedonia as opposed to Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you are not claiming that, in fact, such incident didn't take place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been such incidents, but I'm certainly not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there's a couple of documents I would ask you to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't had time to upload those documents for the simple reason that we received the proofing notes of Mr. Bolton relatively late in the day, but we have copies both -- for the Prosecutor and we will place one copy on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this document will appear on your screen. It will be placed on the ELMO. It is ... do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you look at the -- my own copy having disappeared, I will use the one on the screen. From the bottom of the document you can see it's a document which has been declassified by NATO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will just ask you to focus on the comment or paragraph under the date 8 June 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It records the following incident or the following facts, in any case: "FYROM security forces have undertaken military operations aimed for elimination of the terrorist groups in Kumanovo-Lipkovo region at 5.00 a.m. this morning. FYROM army general staff spokesman, Blagoje Markovski, said such activity continue due to the humanitarian crisis, mainly with water supply crisis and saving of the civilians who are used as a human shield by the terrorists. Markovski informed that the action is continuing and that there are no injured and dead soldiers." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that it suggests that at least on that occasion there was, in fact, use of human shield; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. But I feel that I have to say that one of the problems that we confronted as the international community in Macedonia was reports that came to us either from the Crisis Management Centre or the authorities, as this indeed seems to be, that we then attempted to verify and were unable to do so. There seemed to be a problem with definition of situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, I'll ask the registry to bring up document which is now Exhibit 1D16, that's 1-6. Sir, you will -- it's under tab 13, 1-3, of your binder. You will recall it is an internal OSCE e-mail to Ambassador Stoudmann which records a number of recorded human rights violations by EAAG. And if I ask you to look at point 10 on that list, it says this: "Initiating hostilities in area known to be inhabited by civilians, including children. Videotape of the armed activity in Tetovo immediately prior to the cease-fire shows children playing in the field immediately adjacent to an area from which the EAAG initiated automatic weapons fire and running away in terror as the shooting continues. Eight mortar rounds were dropped almost randomly on the city." Sir, would you agree that this incident in any case would a recorded incident of use of human shield; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to indicate that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we need to tender the NATO documents. I don't think it is particularly useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that on Saturday afternoon - that would be the 11th of August - there was a meeting of village leader in the village of Ljuboten. Is that something that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically I can't say that I was necessarily aware of that meeting. But we did have quite regular telephone contact with villagers at that time and we were aware there were consultations going on amongst villagers as to what they were going to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who Commander Lisi is?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lisi. No I don't recall that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Moving on to another issue which you deal with in your -- in your report of the 15th. I think you've indicated that four houses - and that's the four houses I understand we have discussed earlier - and you say, "This have been the objective of a military assault." Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- I don't actually recall saying it, but it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's in your report?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your understanding was, in fact, that quite a large amount of fire of different sort had been directed at those houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would also be consistent with firing being directed at people inside the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the houses that had been hit and there was no indication of people having been hit there that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that in the fire, in any case, suggests that that's what may have been targeted?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a huge amount of ammunition expended, judging by the amount of empty cases and cardboard cartons for packing ammunition, small arms ammunition, a great deal of it. And thus, the expenditure of that amount of ammunition in an aimed, deliberate manner would indicate to me, if humans were the target, then there would be a great deal of dead humans. There were five. The houses had suffered a great deal of small arms damage at relatively short range. With my military background, I would say that that was either indiscriminate fire or fire from untrained personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think one other thing you said yesterday in your evidence and in any case in your statement was that you saw no signs of fortified defensive positions. I'm not sure I have the right expression. But that was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prepared defensive positions, that's correct, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your evidence, sir, is not that such position did not exist during the week and your evidence is that there was none on the 14th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I must also say that was in the area of the what I would call the tactical operation that occurred on the northern road in the area of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you specify your answer?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Ljuboten is quite a large village. The lower part of the village, I did not examine for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree, I suppose, that had there been a defensive position in the village at the time, that would be indicative of what was in fact happening in the village, that there was in fact military, if I may call it that, exchange between two sides?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe my learned colleague had just -- has just introduced his version of the events and I don't think that is really appropriate. He suggests that had there been a defensive position in the village at that time, that would be indicative of what was in fact happening in the village. There was in fact military. Is that my learned colleagues' interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think the witness has -- the witness has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's all right, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Saxon, you're being a little too sensitive, I would suggest. I can see the thrust of the question. It was a loaded question, but it was directed at a witness well capable of dealing with a loaded question and I think everybody understands the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I unload this one, if I may. But you would agree, Mr. Bolton, that a fortified position could have been removed, if there had been one, any time between the 12th and the 14th when you visited the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now ask to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, going back for a minute to the four buildings which had quite a number of signs of fire, gun-fire. You would agree that those four houses would have been used as a shooting or at least as an observation post or position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not want to indicate that they were, because I have no knowledge to that effect. However, they are on high ground and as such there is a reasonable view of surrounding ground from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would also be consistent with the markings on the house?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The markings on the house are consistent with the house being hit by -- by projectiles from fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And had the house been used as a shooting position? The markings would -- I mean would have been indicative of a return fire; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had they been, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to turn once again to the report of the 16th of August, sir, if I may for a minute. And this is under your tab 2 in your binder. It's 1D24. And I'll ask you kindly to go to page 4 of that document. It would be the fourth paragraph starting with the word "near the field." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the conclusions of the OSCE in its special report on Ljuboten concerning those houses reads as follows: "Near the field where the bodies of the three men were found, there are two complexes of houses. On the right side of the road is a group of four white houses. One of the dead men in the field is the owner of the first white house. On the left and in the immediately area of one body and the field with the other two, is a group of two houses and a barn. The buildings on the left have been burned and have been subject of considerable incoming weapons fire." Sir that's consistent with what you have been telling us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although at one point I did not have that information that the -- one of the dead one in the field was the owner of the first white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the remainder of the information, you would agree it's consistent with yours?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "This building are located where they could be a useful observation point from which to monitor Macedonian movements or direct fire upon them." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, that's not an unreasonable conclusion draw, is it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not. I myself would not use them for that purpose, because they are obviously -- they're quite prominent buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But they might have been?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they may have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, another issue that I would raise with you concerning this issue of defensive position. I think you've indicated, and correct me if I'm wrong, that what you were referring the sort of defensive positions that you had in mind were the sort of defensive position I think you said you saw in other places; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did refer to, I believe, other defensive positions that I'd seen, and I mentioned sandbagged windows and trenches but there can be other forms of prepared defence. I saw no indication of prepared defensive positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were not suggesting that, in your view, there were no villagers with NLA presence in which no search position would exist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, can you say that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: A little bit circumvented. You would agree that there could be villages with NLA presence without search defensive positions?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that one of the tactics of the NLA to take over villages was to incriminate -- incriminent -- incrementally take over the village, insert people in the village, bring in logistics, and bit by bit take over the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: May I ask the registry to bring up document 1D136. And it's ERN 1D001654.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, it's under your tab 34 in your binder. As you can see, it's one of your own documents, if I may so. It comes from the spillover monitor mission to Skopje and its title is Standard Operating Procedures on monitoring and it's dated the 23rd of August. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to focus on the first paragraph of that document. And I will read it out to you. "Ethnic Albanian armed groups EAAG, have taken control of considerable areas of the country and to a large extent held this against counter-offensive operations launched by the government armed forces ARM. The modus operandi of the EAAG by and large to is to occupy ground by infiltration requiring a great deal of preparation before overtly declaring areas under their control. These preparation include the insertion of supplies, arms, and equipment as well as the preparation of the local inhabitants to be receptive to their emergence." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Therefore, there are a number of indicatives, the hardening of the local populations attitude to the government, lots of young men hanging around looking at you suspiciously, or the noticably enhanced security stance of Macedonian forces in the area could suggest that an area is being prepared to be taken over or is ready. The sudden exodus of women and children from a village is also a strong indicator that EAAG activity is imminent. Normally these preparation are done there regions where there is significant population of ethnic Albanians." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to have a look at paragraph 3 below. And in particular with -- if can you see in the middle of that paragraph there is a sentence starting with Skopje, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it say this is: "Skopje has not yet been clearly defined. However, it is apparent that they are dormant members of EAAG in the north of the city. There is also information to suggest that the borders with Albania and Kosovo are very porous. And that traditional smuggling routes are regularly used now by the criminal fraternity to transport the necessary supplies into areas in preparation for future EAAG operations. These areas have also been mined and great care must be exercised when having to operate within them." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what the OSCE standard operating procedure on monitoring says?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D31, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to rely if I may on your ballistic expertise. You've indicated, I think, that you saw, I think you said hundreds of casings of ammunition in the streets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you indicated that most or all of them were of the 762 millimetre calibre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the sort of ammunition which would be used, for instance, for Kalashnikov rifle or gun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the family of Kalashnikov weapons use that calibre, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the Kalashnikov, sir, was a weapon that was used at the time by both sides, the NLA and the Macedonian forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Various models of it from various origins but in effect the same ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is not your evidence, sir, that you were able to determine whether any particular casing that you saw in the village came from one gun rather than the other and by that I mean from either side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would also like to go back an incident which you have recounted yesterday and also recorded, I believe in your statement about what you believe to be diesel spillage on the street; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you indicated that the -- you took this picture because you found the presence of what you believe to be diesel on the street and a smouldering house to be interesting. I don't want to use the inadequate term, but I think it was your expression; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm correct to understand as well that you didn't make any analysis of the spillage on the streets. You just-- it was your guess that it was diesel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But if I may explain why I feel qualified to make that judgment. I spent the first four or five years of my army career in a tank unit, and I regularly spilt diesel all over me. I know very well what it smells like, what it tastes like, and what it feels like; and I believe that what was on the ground then was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that at the time on the 14th it still smelled of diesel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you don't know, sir, who put that diesel on the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Nor when; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you're also aware, sir, that after the events of the 12th a number of houses in the village of Ljuboten were set on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to show you a report which is 1D135. And it's ERN 1D001652. And, sir, it's under your tab 31. You can see it is dated 17th of August, and it comes-- it's sent to operations office Skopje, and it comes from team location Radisani. That would be your team, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that a document you are familiar with? Do you recall that document?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, but it certainly looks to one that comes from our staff, our team, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask you to look at the first section of that document under the time 17. It says: "Team tasked to visit Ljuboten in order to investigate burning houses. It was discovered that one Macedonian house, two Albanian houses, and one Albanian outbuilding had been destroyed by arson." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to describe the incidents in more detail: "At approximately 7.30 the team arrived in the village of Ljuboten to investigate reports of house fires in the area. Investigation established that at approximately midnight on 16/17 August, a Macedonian house on the road leading north-west from the church and some 150 metres from the church had burnt. It was also established that at approximately 11 hours on the 17th August three Albanian properties had also been burnt, one outbuilding, and two adjoining houses, all three on the same road as the Macedonian house." Then I would just like to draw your attention to the last sentence of that paragraph. It says this: "Both Albanian and Macedonian villagers stated that 'army paramilitaries,' and there's parentheses, (both Albanians and Macedonians were clear that the personnel referred to were not police) had been in the area of the village at the time the Albanian properties burnt." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's, as we've indicated a document that would have come from your office in Radisani?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would also like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D32, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like move back one step to the 14th of August, 2001, and your efforts to convince an investigating judge to come in the village. At paragraph 22 of your consolidated statement you recount that the judge to whom you talk through a policeman, we understand, had been advised it would not be safe for him to enter the village with his team. Do you recall having been told that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also turned down an offer which I think you made to him for you to escort him inside the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. We made a sequence of offers, each one of which required negotiation with the Albanians to achieve. There were really two main stages in that. One was to convey the judge in our own vehicles -- three main stages. The second was to convey the judge in our vehicles with a police escort in our vehicles. As I recall it, it was in our vehicles. We offered to carry police, which is unusual for us because we do not carry armed personnel in our vehicles. And the third stage was to have him -- to allow him to be escorted by police in their own vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But as far as you're concerned, is that correct that OSCE doesn't bear any weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, I suppose, that the area at the time was not entirely secure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my judgment, at the time it was secure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, sir, I will ask you to turn back to the report of the 16 of August, and that's again under tab 2 of the report, under -- sorry, under tab 2 of the binder and it is the first page of that document, sir. And it's again Exhibit 1D24. And I will ask you to focus on the very bottom of that page, the last paragraph where the OSCE official report about this incident says this: "It is important to emphasis to anyone contemplating undertaking the full forensic examination of these bodies or scene, that this site is in a conflict area that, although calm on the date of this observation, is not entirely secure." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. You're going to have to direct me again. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is very last sentence on page 1 and goes up to the top of page 2, sir. It's --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. In the italics, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you like me to read it again to you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that's what it says, obviously?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also agree that on the 14th you saw two individuals which you understood and your colleague understood to be members of the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But it does not change the fact that I feel that the area was secure enough for an investigation to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you don't question the fact that someone else could have taken a different view, obviously?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They clearly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, also that the OSCE assisted at a later time with the return of the police in the village of Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that the police did not return until I believe the early days of January of 2002?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The OSCE assisted in re-establishment of regular policing patrols. That was a different situation to the specifically negotiated situation on the 14th, in which we had negotiated with the villagers the access to the village of police and an investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't that correct, sir, that even at the time of the exhumation in April of 2002 at the time when you again had negotiated with the villagers and made all sorts of arrangements, protection, security with NATO, EUMM, OSCE, there was still concerns for the Macedonian participants in that operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was at a different time, but correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll just direct you to one particular document. It's 1D151 and the ERN is 1D001697. And it's under tab 58 in your ... Sir, we might come back to that document at a later stage, if time permits. But you will see from it that it is essentially a draft operational plan for the Ljuboten exhumation and it was drafted by Mr. Tucker and amended by Mr. Smith. Can you see that on the top of the document? That should be your tab 58.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 58. Sorry. I was on 57. I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the page I would like to draw your attention is the fourth page of the document is that would be ERN 1770. There's a particular paragraph, sir, which relates to the forming up point for the exhumation party, as it's called. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says this: "Due to the security considerations of the members of the forensic institute, the exhumation party rendezvous at the field station of OSCE (Henry Bolton) at location. It is imperative that all party involved in this convoy are at the RV point in time for the proposed coordinated departure." So you would agree at that time that obviously there were still security concern for those people, the forensic experts, or in any case that they had expressed those concerns to you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be -- the issue was a sensitive one, and it was necessary and we considered necessary to take all measures we could to ensure that this whole activity was professionally organised and tightly organised, thereby removing -- or decreasing any chance of something going wrong, including people getting lost, going down the wrong road. There's a need to organise the event. And that's what this document was for and that's why we had the RV and why we wanted to ensure that everybody was together and left together.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's also why, sir, NATO provided security for the operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: NATO provided security for the operation, that is correct. NATO provided security for a number of activities, and they had their own mandate. You would have to speak to them about that. But that is not-- it was due to the profile of this event and the whole exhumation process and the publicity it was receiving. The situation was very different to the situation that existed on the 14th in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree, sir, that it's actually upon the request, the express request of the OTP that security was provided by NATO?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that does not give us an indication of the threat level.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to the issue of the actual exhumation sir. And I understand that yourself were involved in some aspects of this matter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some aspects of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll deal with that in due course. But, sir, I take it a step back so Their Honours understand perhaps a bit of the process that led up to that. You were aware, no doubt, of the efforts that were being made by the authority to organise this exhumation, and I will ask the registry perhaps to bring up, that's Rule 65 ter 109 and the ERN is 7332 ET. And, sir, it is under your tab 43. I will just go back to my original question, sir. Were you aware of the efforts being made by various Macedonian authorities to organise an exhumation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like you to focus on this particular document here. As you can see, it comes from the Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior and it's dated 7 September 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a matter of clarification, this document or at least a version of it already in evidence as P55. The reason why we're using this one is there is a dating mistake which I think way pointed out earlier. It referred to the 7th of August instead of the 7 of September, which is clearly wrong, so we prefer to use the correct translation in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, would you confirm that this is being sent to the public prosecutor's office, Skopje, and to the duty investigative judge of lower courts, Skopje II?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry to be precise. I can see that that's to whom it's addressed. I can't say that it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I appreciate you being precise. And the title of the document suggests that it's a motion. It's been interpreted as a motion or recommendation for exhumation and autopsy, motion for exhumation and autopsy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask the -- ask you and the registry to turn to the last page of this document, you can see that it has been signed by the director, Mr. Goran Mitevski. Do you know who Mr. Mitevski was at that time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he was director of the public security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I draw your attention to the last paragraph on that page, it says the following: "Due to the aforementioned, we believe that the motion for exhumation and autopsy is justified and should be accepted with the aim of identifying the five corpses and the establishing the cause of death of the five individuals from the village of Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of that particular motion or suggestion, recommendation which was being made by Mr. Mitevski on the 7th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, were you aware of the fact that this motion or recommendation had been made on behalf or at the behest of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. And I have not seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if Your Honour wants to admit this document separately or if Your Honour would prefer that perhaps the translation issue whether this document may perhaps replace the one with the -- Can we tender -- I'm advised by my reliable colleague that perhaps we should try to tender that version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, do you have any view?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Given the error that was apparently made, no, Your Honour, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As exhibit 1D33, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I will ask you now look at a different document which is under tab 44 of your binder, and it is D176, and the ERN number is 1D001904. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see from the first page of the document it's again a document that comes from the Ministry of Interior, and its title is "Information about the events in the vicinity of the Skopje village Ljuboten." And the place and date are Skopje, November 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask you, sir, to go directly to the last page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the registry's benefit, that would be page 1918.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd ask to you look at the last paragraph. It says this: "Having in consideration the importance of the exhumation as the investigative act, in order to resolve the reasons for their death, the ministers of interior -- the minister of interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski, immediately after the case has submitted the written recommendation to the principal public prosecution office, Skopje II in Skopje to start conducting the process of exhumation of corpse of the people in order to continue with post-mortem and thorough examination." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you have indicated you didn't have that information at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was aware there were numerous -- there was -- there were various moves and pressures being applied and so on to ensure that an investigation took place, but I wasn't privy to these documents or the discussions that led to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that perhaps after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. We will have the first break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, two quick matters of clarifications for the record. The first one is in relation to document 1D33, which we just tendered as a separate document. My legal assistant is indeed very reliable. That was counsel that was not so reliable understanding the message. There seems to be two documents, two separate documents with two dates, one of the 7 of August and one of the 7 of September. The one of the 7 of August was dealt by my colleague with the previous witness. As for the document we've tendered, it's the same document as P55 with a different translation. Your Honour will see there are a difference of wording. Ours is the CLSS translation and the Prosecution version is, as I understand it, an internal translation. The second matter, Your Honour, if I may, would be to simply tender the last document which I showed to the witness before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, subject to Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may, perhaps my colleague could provide us can some chain of custody information regarding this last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With pleasure, we received it from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it's got to come from a reliable source, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll leave that judgement to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, we're just helping Mr. Saxon at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter document 1D176 will become Exhibit 1D34, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bolton, you've indicated and fairly so, that did you not have specific knowledge of the previous document that I've showed you. However, were you aware of public calls made by Mr. Boskoski for an exhumation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall them, but I'm certainly not going to indicate that they did not occur, but I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I may, sir, I'll show you a particular document which is a -- again Rule 65 ter 130, and the ERN is N0009212. And, sir, it's under your tab 45, I believe. As you will see, sir, it appears to be a press article dated 15th of August, 2001, and the title is "FYROM Interior Minister Boskoski expresses satisfaction with OSCE attitude. First, perhaps, let me ask you this: Were you aware of the fact that Mr. Boskoski met with Ambassador Ungaro very shortly after the event at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you aware of the fact that following that meeting, the two of them had a sort of a press conference?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do vaguely recall a press conference, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I may ask to you go into the middle of that document to a paragraph which starts with the word "this discussion," can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this is a statement which is attributed to Mr. Boskoski. It says this: "This discussion was motivated by the murder of five terrorists that were dressed in civilian clothing when found; namely, the Macedonian security forces were not allowed to approach the dead for two days in order to do the investigation on-site along with the public prosecutor and investigation judge." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if you go further down in this document, there is a paragraph starting with the words "about the affair." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It say this is: "About the affair in Ljuboten, Boskoski informed that by the time the expert time had arrived on site, the bodies were already buried." And then there is a statement which is attributed to him: "In order to know the truth an exhumation, acknowledged by the public prosecutor, will have to take place." Can you see I can?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a statement which is attributed to Ambassador Ungaro which says this: "The misunderstanding occurred as a result of the intentional or unintentional misinterpretations of OSCE information for the foreign media." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then is being recorded as saying this: "We do not make judgements in advance. If we get some information through our observers on site, we share this with the Macedonian authorities first and advise them to do some research in which we are ready to assist." And it goes on to say: "OSCE Ambassador to Macedonian asked Ljube Boskoski to make the whole investigation of the affair of Ljuboten be as transparent as possible in the name of justice." Were you aware of such reports in the Macedonian press at the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very many reports in the Macedonian press at that time. This particular one I don't recall, but it would seem to be an account of what happened and does not contradict my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall as well that the competent judicial authorities of Macedonia actually continued to attempt to organise this exhumation operation in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in that, and I -- I can't answer that question. All I can say is that there were efforts from a number of international agencies and in working -- working with the Macedonian authorities to progress an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And -- well, I'm going to show you a document and ask you whether that's information you had in your possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is 1D175 and the ERN number is 1D001895.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
