utterances.text: And, sir, I believe it is under tab 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record this document is the same as P99 which has already been admitted. We understand that P99 does not contain a translation, a Macedonian translation of the English, and that the English may in fact be a translation of a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, sir, I'd ask you to look first at the first page of that document. And you will see it comes from the public prosecutions of the Republic of Macedonia and it has a number, A number 231/01 and it's dated 18 of November 2001, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of the document, sir, is information on the events happened in the area of the village Ljuboten, Skopje, in the period August 10, 11, 12, and the 14, 2001. Sir, at this stage I would simply ask to you go to the third and last page or third of four pages, sorry. That's the page which has a signature on it.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you can see it has been signed by Mr. Stavre Dzikov, who at the time was the state or public prosecutor of Macedonia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name of the public prosecutor, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Fair enough. I'll just ask to you focus on the middle paragraph on that page starting with the words: "Since the bodies." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it reads like that: "Since the bodies were already buried and there was no autopsy done over them, in accordance to Article 244, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the criminal procedural law, the public prosecutor, on the basis of Article 148, paragraph 1 of the quoted law, submitted a proposal to the competent magistrate judge for certain investigative measures to be taken. For an exhumation, examination, and an autopsy of the bodies in order to confirm the identity of the five buried bodies. The reason of the death, time of the time, and the circumstances in which the death appeared. It was proposed that this procedure is carried out by the forensic and criminalistic institute within the faculty of medicine in Skopje." Sir, at the time were you aware of that particular request having been made by the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have some recollection of being informed of it, but it's vague.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct also that sometimes in November of 2001, the chief Prosecutor of this Tribunal visited Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, or at least information which you had in your possession, that at the time the Macedonian authorities sought the assistance of the Office of the Prosecutor to carry out this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will recall, however, that the Prosecution, the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, in the course of November 2001 got in touch with your organisation in relation to the exhumation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware that the OSCE provided assistance, and I can only presume that that was as a result of an agreement. But if that was the case, I was not party to that agreement or the discussions leading to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll perhaps ask you then to look at document 1D142. That would be ERN 1D001674, and that's under the tab 49 of your binder. As you can see, sir, is this is something called "investigators notes," and it's such -- it basically is again the record, as you will see, of a meeting between members of the OSCE and members of the Office of the Prosecutor. And it says that the purpose of the meeting in question was arranged by Mr. Andre Sidlik [phoen], operation officer ICTY, for the visit of Mr. Dennis Milner, deputy chief of investigations. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the time and date of the meeting is recorded as 9.45 Tuesday, 27th November 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the location is offices of the OSCE in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct? And then it lists the person present during that meeting, and I understand they are three persons from the OSCE, Sandra Mitchell, senior member OSCE. Andre Palmer, political advisor. Maurice Kanavan, senior monitor OSCE. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would understand that those people were colleagues of yours at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they worked in a different location. They worked in the mission headquarters, but yes. We were all in the same mission, and we knew each other, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's the name of three people from the Office of the Prosecutor. I don't need to go through them at this stage, but you can see them for yourself. And you will also notice, sir, that there seems to be no member of the Macedonian authorities at the meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would appear to be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can now just go to the first paragraph of that document on the first page, starting with the word: "Mr. Dennis Milner, DM introduced the representatives of the ICTY to those present. He stated the reason for his visit was a follow-up to that of the Prosecutor." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just before we turn the page, you will see that all of the participants had been given initials when they're being referred to the in the text. MC stands, for instance, for Maurice Kanavan and SM for Ms. Sandra Mitchell. If I can just ask you to turn to the next page, sir. And ask you to focus on the third paragraph of that document which started with MC, that would your colleague Mr. Kanavan. Maurice Kanavan stated that from his point of view, the aim of his unit was to assist the security forces, police, to re-enter villages such as Ljuboten. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we then did confirm earlier that at the time that was one of the thing that OSCE was attempting to assist with was the return of the police in certain areas including Ljuboten, right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct; although, I'm not certain that we'd actually started to do that on a regular programmatic basis at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think-- I think -- would it be fair to say that it's one of your colleague, Mr. Seford, deputy head of the mission at the time who prepared the, if I may call it that, the matrix of the return together with the Minister of Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That -- that's correct, yes. And it would have been sometimes, perhaps in December of 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I believe, yes. Around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask you now to turn to a paragraph further down this document, and it starts with the word -- well, it's the last paragraph, sir, of this page, and the comments are attributed to DM, which is Dennis Milner of the ICTY. And what Mr. Milner is recorded as saying is this: "It was vital that ICTY investigators obtain access to these areas to conduct their investigations." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the previous sentence you will see that "these locations," refer to Neprosteno and Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would not -- I would like now to ask you to focus on a position attributed to a member of your organisation and that's Sandra Mitchell. That's the paragraph just above the one I've just read, and it's recorded as this: "Sandra Mitchell stated there were clear human rights issues involved in investigations. She sated that the OSCE did not have a clear human rights mandate and did not have any employees in the field with sufficient human rights experience. Great care would have to be shown by the OSCE. She also stated that the OSCE would cooperate fully with the ICTY. However, apart from the ambush of Macedonian security forces of -- in May 2001, the OSCE did not have any file of interest to the ICTY to hand over." And there's another statement attributed to Ms. Sandra Mitchell on the next page which I would like to point out to you. It's the third paragraph, sir. It start SM again: "Sandra Mitchell again stated the importance, in her view, of ICTY involvement in the judicial process. She suggested the possibility of the ICTY providing guidance and/or advice to the Macedonian judicial authorities on the review, preparation, and subsequent prosecution of suspects within the jurisdiction of the authorities." Can you see?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, were you informed at the time of those meetings, or did you receive any general information that such meetings had taken place?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of meetings. I was not aware of their content.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D35, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, were you also aware that a number of subsequent meetings took place in relation to the same matter?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to meetings between the OSCE and ICTY --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I don't think we'll have the time to go through them at this stage, but would it correct to say that you personally assisted in some respect the Office of the Prosecution, in particular Mr. Tucker, with a number of matters pertaining to the exhumation? Perhaps can I be more precise. You visited-- did you visit the location together with Mr. Tucker at one stage?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one stage, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I'd like to move on because we have to now add a bit forward in time to the beginning of the year 2002, still dealing with the issue of exhumation. I'd like to show you a document which is number 1D146 with the ERN 1D001686 and that's number 53 in your binder. Sir, again this is a letter which comes from the public prosecutor office of the Republic of Macedonia with a number 14-2002 and it's dated 22nd January of 2002. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's being sent to OSCE monitoring mission to the Republic of Macedonia, Ambassador Mr. Craig Janis [phoen], Skopje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you confirm that by this stage Mr. Janis had replaced Ambassador Ungaro at the head of your mission?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, if I may ask you, perhaps, to focus on the top right-hand corner of this document. There's a handwritten annotation. Would you be able to decipher those for us?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below the N number you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first one appears to say HOM which I would understand to be head of mission/DHOM, deputy head of mission/AR, I do not recall. That is not a common abbreviation in the OSCE, and I can't recall at this time what it may be. And then under that there is something that I suspect is

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Palmer --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Which would be Andrew Palmer?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Andrew Palmer, who --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was a member of the mission at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the head of mission, deputy head of mission, and this AR would that be the persons to whom the letter would be transmitted by Mr. Palmer; is that what we should understand it to be?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would understand it differently. I would understand it that whoever annotated this document with those abbreviations and with

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Palmer was the person who intended the document to be copied to them including Mr. Palmer. That's what I would understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. That's helpful, thank you. If we can go into the text of that letter, sir, to the first paragraph you can see that it relates to the events in the village of Ljuboten on 10, 11, and 12 August 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also refers to a case number for that events as RO number 1098-01. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says that this case as opened in the public prosecutor's office, Skopje. And that it was being prosecuted by public prosecutor Dragoljub Jakic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the purpose of the letter is in the second paragraph of that letter and it says: "I would like to invite you to the preliminary working meeting which will be held on 30 January 2002, at 1500 hours, Wednesday, in the premise of the public prosecutor's office of the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the signatory of that letter which would be again be Mr. Jakic, public prosecutor, says that all further activities of the prosecution, the court, and the forensics department with regards to determining the victims in the Ljuboten events will be determined at the working meeting. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D36, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of the fact that one such meeting, in fact, took place subsequently?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subsequent to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: To this letter. Subsequently to the letter, yes.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, in other words --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As a result of the letter.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Specifically, no; in general I'm aware that they were planning meetings with the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we move in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to look at another document which relates to the same issue and that's under tab 61 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the registry's benefit, that's 1D154, ERN 1D001705.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, that's a document which has been disclosed to us again by the Office of the Prosecutor. It's a UN -- a NATO declassified or unclassified document, and as you can see from the title it relates to the Ljuboten case, ICTY investigation, and that's dated the 30th of January 2002. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then there's EUMM meeting for Ljuboten case. And again the first sentence record the following: "On 30 January 2002 EUMM attended a meeting at the public prosecution department regarding events in Ljuboten on 10, 12 August. Among those present were deputy public prosecutor Cakic, professor Aleksander Duma of the department of forensic medicine and president of appealation court Ms. Filimana Manevska [phoen], Mr. Andrej Silik of the ICTY, Ambassador Klaus Verlis [phoen] of NATO, EUMM and OSCE represented the international community." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Prosecutor Stavre Dzikov, it continues, "chaired the meeting, the local authorities explained very briefly that the security forces had acted against terrorists in Ljuboten during three days from 10 to 12 August 2001 after a mine incident in the area on 10 August." Then it goes on to record a number of facts, and as you will see, this document also contains the comments, the personal comments of the EUMM representative that was present at the meeting. And we have already gone over that, so I won't. But I will ask to you turn to the next page, if you can. And first I'd like to ask you, sir, if you could explain what Amber Fox is?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amber Fox was the NATO monitoring mission at the time. A strange name, I grant you, but that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they were present in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you to focus your attention on the last paragraph of that page which is entitled "Ljuboten exhumation" with a date of 5 April. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It starts by saying: "Start for the Ljuboten exhumation, start tomorrow?"

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I may have the wrong one. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be page number 2 of the document. It has the number 1D001706 --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- on the top. And that will be the last, if you will --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. My mistake, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "OSCE, EUMM and ICTY are ready on the ground. The exhumation is going to be performed by the public prosecutor under supervision by the ICTY in a way so it is done by international standards." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "No interference is expected from the MOI but MOI activities in other areas are expected in order to distract the attention away from the media." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a comment, which is attributed to amber fox or NATO HQ and it says this: "Offered" -- "Offers made by MOI Boskoski to provide the area with security were rejected on the basis of his possible indictment by the ICTY since the mass grave is related to the incidents that happened in this village on 10 August," end of comment. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that the offers of assistance of Mr. Boskoski had been declined in this matter?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware that there had been offers of assistance, but that there was general concern, as I understood it, for -- to avoid too much of an overt policing presence in that area at the time, in order to -- to not give the situation too high a profile and maybe create tension.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the exhumation process, in fact, went without a hitch, is that correct, it went well?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware. I was not a party to that. Some of my monitors were, and as far as I'm aware, there was no problem there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And no interference?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No interference.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to a different subject, sir. You have mentioned a number of contacts, I believe, which you had with a number of members of the Ministry of Interior. Would it be correct that you generally had a good working relationship with the local police with whom you dealt?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've named two particular individuals with whom you had regular contacts, Mr. Petre Stojanovski and Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, you had a good and friendly relationship with these two individuals?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I would -- that's a correct description, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are on a first-name basis with those two individuals?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Later on in time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have also indicated I believe that on a number of occasion when you encountered difficulties in the context of your work, for instance, to pass through check-points, you sometimes called Mr. Bliznakovski with a view for him to assist you with going through those check-points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. If I can add to that: We carried identification and these cards that the monitors, OSCE monitors carried were intended to demonstrate that we had freedom of movement. Often it was the case that local police who were often reservists on check-points would obstruct that movement. They felt they were doing their jobs. We, rather than discussing the issue with them, would intervene with what we felt was the appropriate level in the chain of command to ensure they were given the appropriate information at that time thereby allowing us to move through, and that was the reason for the contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So the person in the chain of command which you understood to be capable of that was Mr. Bliznakovski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that the passes you've just mentioned were delivered to you by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of -- one of them were. We carried a lot of passes. But, yes, the Ministry of Interior issued us with one of those passes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware, sir, of the fact that on a number of occasion the OSCE headquarter either through its ambassador or its deputy had expressed its satisfaction and gratitude to the Ministry of Interior and Mr. Boskoski in particular for his assistance?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll then ask you to have a look at document 62 in your binder, and it is a document ID155, with an ERN 1D001920. And the Macedonian is 1D155, 1D001919. The reason why I mention the Macedonian is the original appears to have been the Macedonian because it bears a signature and an annotation at the top of the letter. Sir, if I can go through that letter briefly with you. You can see it's being addressed to Mr. Boskoski as Minister of the Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the address at the top of the letter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it's dated Skopje, 14 June 2001. And it is directed to "My dear minister," and it goes on to say this: "Please allow me to express my deepest personal gratitude and respect and that of the OSCE mission for the exceptional level of understanding, cooperation, readiness and efficiency which you and all the members of your valued ministry have always demonstrated during our mutual contact. The permits given by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia to our personnel, international and local, are of critical importance for the work and functioning of the office of the OSCE mission in the Republic of Macedonia in accordance with our mandate." And if you go to the bottom of the letter you will see that it has been signed by the deputy head with a spelling mistake which might be a result of the Cyrillic being translated into English, but that's Mr. Robin Seford, the head of mission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deputy head of mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Deputy head of mission. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will ask to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As 1D38, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I now wish to turn to a separate part of your evidence in your statement which related to matters that you have observed in your capacity as a head of your office in Radisani. You've indicated, I think, in your statement that you had arrived sometimes towards the end of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated, I think, that you arrived about six weeks prior to the incident?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification, sir: You were not being employed as a consultant by the authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: By the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, no .

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Nor were you an employee of the ministry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you worked solely for and on behalf of the OSCE; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking you, sir, is in the statement comment is attributed to you to that the effect that you worked within the ministry. I simply wanted to the clarify this with you.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I assist with that. Later I was employed as a consultant in Macedonia, and in that role I worked within the compound of the Ministry of Interior on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that that was later in time? Was it 2002 or 2003?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2003, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Sir, at the time could you, so that we have an idea of where your offices stand in the OSCE hierarchy, can you indicate who was your immediate superior at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OSCE is not necessarily a simple beast to understand. The -- I reported, in theory, directly to the head of mission. However, the paper reporting system to enable the paper to be managed in a reasonable manner was correlated by the coordination cell. We had a director of field operations. We had a deputy head of mission who oversaw that process. So in effect, the reporting -- our reports went through a more circuitous route than, if you like, the policy instruction coming down, although that could follow both routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And geographically, then -- and I'm -- am I correct to understand that what you call your AOR, area of responsibility, was the Skopje area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the entire Skopje area, as would be understood from looking at the old regional administrative boundaries, but effectively -- effectively, the northern, and practically speaking, it was Skopje city, slightly south of that and to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So it wasn't a nation-wide coverage; is that correct? It was this limited part of the Skopje area?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: For my team it was a limited area of responsibility, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've indicated already that it was very important for you in your role and capacity to have contacts in that area and at your level to assist with your mission and those contacts where at times with Mr. Bliznakovski and Stojanovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But just as a point of clarification with regards your earlier question, there were occasions when we deployed - I don't know whether this is important - but there were occasions when we deployed teams outside that area of responsibility to support teams in Tetovo or Kumanovo. But your second point, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also have contacts, as I understand, lower down the chain of command with the local police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and my teams had regular contact with members -- employees of the Ministry of Interior, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've -- you can confirm that you had no contacts at the ministerial level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you never met with minister -- then-minister Boskoski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't then and -- no, I had not then, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you have any contacts, professional contacts with Goran Mitevski, you remember he is the director of public security?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you have any contacts with the head of the crime police Mr. Zivko Petrovski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated, however, I think, in your statement that you had some contacts with Mr. Zoran Jovanovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was subsequent to the events that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that you have met him perhaps once or twice in the year 2001? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm going ask your memory a lot there, but would it be correct that your first meeting with Petre Stojanovski took place perhaps on the 13th or 14th of August? Would that be correct, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I cannot recall, but I don't think it was quite that early.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you think it might have been a little bit later?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and we're probably talking days or weeks later, but I -- I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would that be the case also with Mr. Bliznakovski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to recall when. Let me explain the difficulty that I'm having. When we set up team centre, we realised -- or I realised very rapidly that we required good relations with the police, as this letter from Mr. Seford appears to verify. In order to do our job, we needed to have a good working relationship and that was something that I was keen to establish. I do not recall -- I recall that we established that with Mr. Bliznakovski and with Mr. Stojanovski, but I do not recall when we initiated our contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But would it be fair to say that one of the reasons for that was that during the month of July, I think you've indicated, you were focused primarily on the situation in Radusha; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radusha was an area of concern. There were others. Radusha was one of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In your statement you are recorded as saying the following: "Mr. Boskoski, during the summer of 2001 and subsequently was able to involve himself in an operational matter within the MOI at any level if he so wished." I'm going to ask you a few questions about this, but you also are recorded as saying this: "Very senior members of the MOI would sometimes defer to Mr. Boskoski for decisions concerning issues that involved low-level tactical policing [realtime transcript read in error "tackle police"] Is that correct? That's what you were recorded?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding, yes. I wasn't in meetings between police officials, but that is my understanding of the situation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you actually indicate the basis for this belief of yours by -- or with reference to two particular incidents, and please correct me if I misrepresent those in any way. These are summaries of what you are recorded as saying. The first incident which is attributed to you is that on one occasion, Ljupco Bliznakovski, commander of the Skopje police, and General Jovanovski -- Zoran Jovanovski once told that you only the minister had the authority to make adjustments to police shift assignments due to the fact that shift patterns were established in ministerial directives and regulations. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fair summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I interrupt, Mr. Mettraux, before something goes off the screen. 72, line 13, I think my screen shows you asking a question involving "low-level tackle policy." Was it "tactical policy?"

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think anyone was involved in tackling. It would have been tactical, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It could have been an important issue and I thought it better to correct it --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- before we lose it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, the second incident or event which is referred to in your statement in relation to those assertions, statements attributed to you is an example where you were apparently once told that the minister would in some cases be responsible for deciding upon the removal of police check-points. Do you recall mentioning that particular incident to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall mentioning it to the Office of the Prosecutor, but I remember the incident in which I was told this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd just like to understand your statement a bit better. But your evidence, sir, is that you did not witness either incident yourself. They were recounted to you by others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- in the latter incident that you refer to, we, the OSCE, felt that it was dangerous to the personnel within a police check-point for it to remain where it was. We -- I proposed that it be moved to a location that would enable it to continue doing its job but would offer the personnel within it, the Ministry of Interior employees within it, greater safety and security. I was informed that that was not possible because it was part of a strategic plan that required the ministers' approval to remove it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you remember who told you that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was General Zoran Jovanovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you didn't verify that information, sir, whether there was any such thing as this policy in question?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't in a position to explore that policy further.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Nor is that your evidence, sir -- and I'm just trying to establish what is your evidence. You are not suggesting that Mr. Boskoski was either required or legally responsible for moving check-points from one place to the other?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that in any organisation where a person in the management chain exerts decision making or an influence over decision making in that way, then there is an amount of responsibility. I would consider that within the OSCE, the British Army, or any other organisation to be the case. So I cannot say that there was no -- that he was not responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps my question should be better phrased. It's not your evidence, sir, by law or by any policy you could have access to Mr. Boskoski was the competent person or organ to order the moving or removing of check-points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is correct is that I believe now and I believed then that the -- those people responsible for -- that responsibility for that check-point and others should have been devolved to lower-level tactical commanders. That certainly did not appear to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But from your own observation, sir, you have never seen an order, a decision or a body of rules which would place that particular responsibility on to the Ministry of Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I have not seen anything in writing to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, I mean you have indicated that you have never heard Mr. Boskoski or witnessed Mr. Boskoski give an order or requests, search, the removal of a check-points or the setting up of one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And moving on to the other issue which you have identified in your statement concerning the police shifts, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, sir, it is not your evidence -- and again I don't mean to be critical here. I'm trying to assess the nature of your evidence. But you did not personally saw or witness Mr. Boskoski giving any order or signing any documents in relation to police shifts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, it was made -- I was made aware on a number of occasions that it was by ministerial directive that shift patterns were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I was coming to that, and I'm grateful. But you've actually never seen this directive or this regulation?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, well, I would like to show you a statement which was taken by the Defence and it's ID158. It's ERN number 1D001712, and it's under tab number 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record this is a statement which the Defence has taken from Mr. Ljupco Bliznakovski, which has mentioned already on a number of occasion. We have had Mr. Bliznakovski sign the original document in his own language. That's the Macedonian. The translation which is now on your screen is unofficial translation of -- made by the Defence. As Your Honour knows, we have had regular contact with the CLSS in relation to translation issues. And there was one particular translation matter which we raised with them. At this stage we're still discussing this with the CLSS, and as soon as we get the correct translation or as soon as we resolve this matter with the CLSS, we'll then put on the official translation or we will verify the statement. We will have the statement verified in English translated to Mr. Bliznakovski and signed by him. But this is the situation at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to you look at paragraph 3 of the statement of Mr. Bliznakovski. It says this: "Asked who was responsible for organising of the police shifts at the time, I can say that it was the responsibility of the commanders of the police stations. If there was need for consultation of a question in the area of police works, upwards in the hierarchy, responsible for traffic, criminal, and operative works, public peace and order JRM, it was SVR Skopje. And, sir, SVR Skopje is Mr. Bliznakovski, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he is saying that the responsibility for police shifts falls primarily on police stations and in case of problems, on to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at paragraph 4 it says this: "The Minister of Interior had no role in organising, deciding or preparing police shifts and I know of no example where the minister of the interior took any interest or was involved in the matter of police shifts. Those were purely operative matters which were not within the competence of the SVR. And at paragraph 5 it says: "I never suggested to anyone that the minister of the interior would be competent to deal with such secondary operative matters, as noted above, that was solely the responsibility of SVR." Sir, I think in your statement you recalled Mr. Bliznakovski as being among those who told that you story. Could it be that this version of events which was given to you might have been given to you by someone else?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that the information provided by Mr. Bliznakovski is in contradiction with your recounting or recalling of the matter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that there's contradiction there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage we just ask that this document be marked for identification. I will come back to it a bit later, and also it has not -- as I pointed out, there is an issue of translation and there's another statement which will be referred to later. And we will seek at a later time to tender it through Rule 92 bis, so we will have to go through the process of certification. So at this stage, we simply ask that the document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D39, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, before the transcript disappears in front of our eyes, I'm recorded as when reading paragraph 4 of the statement as reading that saying that "those matter were not within the competence," and either I misread or was misunderstood. But it says: "Those were purely operative matters which were within the competence of the SVR," that's the last sentence of paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd also like to refer to the evidence of another witness who's given evidence before this Trial Chamber. It's witness M 36 and it can be found at page 824. It's not, unfortunately, and I apologise, in your binder. I will read the passage to you, but it's 824 of the transcript. It's a witness who has appeared already in the context of this trial. And he say this: I think it was not the head of the police station was setting them, that is the length of shifts, but the superior officers depending on the situation. So the shift might be increased or reduced depending on the assessment of the security situation and depending on the staffing that was able to the police station. So there again, sir, we have in evidence which is slightly different from both yours and Mr. Bliznakovski, but the understanding of this witness, M 36, is that the responsibility for police shifts was either with the police station or with superior officers within that station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it appears to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd now like to move on to another matter which you have discussed in your statement and that's that you were once told - and I summarised the incidents a bit earlier - that you were once told in one particular incident that the minister himself, Mr. Boskoski, had insisted that a particular check-point should stay where it was. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, sir, and again I'm not meaning to criticise you for this or not suggesting it was your duty, but you did not verify whether or not Mr. Boskoski had indeed made that request; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, with the risk of repeating myself, you never saw a decision of a minister or witnessed the Minister making a request either this one or a request to the same effect; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn your attention once again to the statements of Mr. Bliznakovski, which I think you still have in front of you, and ask you to focus on paragraph 6 of that statement, the second sentence. It says this: "The primary responsibility for those, that is the check-points, would be at the level of the police SVR." And again, sir, that would be the level at which Mr. Bliznakovski was operating; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Those were the authorities that knew and were competent to decide whether a check-point was necessary or needed or whether it should be removed. Ultimately, from a hierarchical point of view, the professional responsibility for such matters would go up to the head of the uniformed police; although, I do not know of a single example where the head of the uniformed police in the MOI was required or requested to intervene in relation to such matters." And then, sir, using your memory, can you recall who was the head of the uniformed police at the time?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could it be Mr. Galevski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And going on with the paragraph of Mr. Bliznakovski, he says this: "I am aware that the matter of check-points was also discussed at the Crisis Management Committee; and thus, in cooperation between the government and the international organisation, OSCE, that were present at the time in Macedonia." Are you also aware, sir, of the fact that the issue of the check-points was at times discussed at the Crisis Management Committee or Centre?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was regularly discussed there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is another statement, sir, which I would like to show to you at this stage, and it's --

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, it's a little embarrassing. I don't not know whether it's possible to take a one - or two-minute break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll do better than that, I think. We will have our second break now, resuming at a quarter to 1.00 and that will then give us a full hour for the last session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we restart three very short matters about documents which have been shown to this witness. There are three documents which have been used with this witness. The first one is under tab 58. I will not seek to tender this document at this stage Your Honour. It's the record of a meeting -- sorry, it's the draft operational plan for the Ljuboten exhumation. We will put that document through a future witness, Mr. Tucker, who's scheduled to testify on behalf of the Prosecution. There is another document, which is under tab 61 in the binder, that's 1D154 and it's a NATO declassified or unclassified document, and I would seek to tender this one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. In order to keep all options open for the Prosecution, with respect to tab 58 that my colleague has just mentioned, the draft operational plan, there was always at least a possibility that the witness, who I believe my colleague is thinking about, may not testify given time constraints et cetera, et cetera. The Prosecution will not oppose tendering this document at this time if my colleague prefers to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I think, Your Honour they are two matters. Obviously if the Prosecution does not object to the tendering, it would be acceptable to us to tender it. The other issue, Your Honour, is if the Prosecution has now taken the position that this witness, Mr. Tucker, will not come, we should be immediately advised of that fact and by immediately I mean before the present witness has finished his testimony. If Mr. Tucker is not to appear to as a witness in this case, I'm quite afraid that there would be a great deal more questions for this particular witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can well image that prospect. Let us deal with the documents first while Mr. Saxon is considering your last comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With pleasure, Your Honour, and I will briefly -- I think we have an agreement in relate -- with the Prosecution in relation to the last document. It's the document under tab 39 and it's 1D175. It's information about the Ljuboten event which I've shown to this witness. The English version of that document is to be found in K 99 which has already been admitted in evidence. However, the Macedonian version which is part of P 99 appears to be an Macedonian translation of the English which is itself a translation of an original Macedonian. We have identified, located the original Macedonian documents, and what we would propose to do, if it's acceptable obviously, to Your Honours, would be to replace the Macedonian translation in effect of that document with our original, and I think the Prosecution agrees with that proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, on that assumption, are you saying that the original is at tab 39 now?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you'd like that now to be received as the actual exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what we would propose is since P99 is already in evidence, in order not to have twice the same document, what we would propose, if that's acceptable, is to -- if you're unplugging the Macedonian translation or -- sorry, the Macedonian original into P99. If I wasn't clear at this stage, the Macedonian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, that's clear, with the consent of the Prosecution, the original Macedonian document will become part of Exhibit P 99 in place of the Macedonian language version that presently forms part of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the court officer will put me in my place later if that's technically impossible, and we'll sort it out. Now, two other documents you've mentioned, and we need to deal with them. First is at tab 58.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With my consent, you'd like to tender that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll tender it if there is no objection at this stage. It was 1D151, 1D0021697 to 17.000. And for the record, it is the proposed draft operational plan for Ljuboten exhumation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D40, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the other document, Your Honour, is under tab 61 of your binder. And it's 1D154 with an ERN 1D001705 to 1706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go back to the issues that we were discussing before, which is the issue of the check-points you will recall.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask you to turn to tab 70, 7-0, of your binder and ask the registry's assistance to bring up document 1D159 with an ERN 1D001717 and, sir, this is a statement taken by representatives of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski from a person named Vojislav Zafirovski. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, for the record, Your Honour, this at this stage is an unofficial translation made by the Defence, and we will follow the same procedure as mentioned earlier. Either we will have the statement read back to Mr. Zafirovski and signed by him, or we will seek a translation from the CLSSs. An official translation that is. Sir if you can have a look at paragraph 3 of the document, it describes in a rather lengthy paragraph the professional duties and responsibilities of Mr. Zafirovski. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you see that he was first employed by the Ministry of Interior in 1978. And up to this day, for 28 years, has been working in various capacities within that ministry. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In relation to the check-point, sir, I would like to ask you to focus on paragraph 5 of the statement of Mr. Zafirovski, and it says this: "The Ministry of Interior is not responsible for deciding of the location and the need for police check-points. The primary authority and responsibility for positioning and removing of check-points is within the heads of the sectors of internal affairs, the heads of the department of internal affairs, head of the larger municipality police stations, or the commander of the local police stations. Furthermore, theoretically there might be instances where regarding these matters the head of the uniformed police to be consulted or even authorised for deciding even though I do not know if that has happened in practice during the crisis in 2001." Sir, once again, Mr. Zafirovski indicates that ultimately, the last person who would be responsible for the issue of locating and the need of police check-points would be the head of the uniformed police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he's saying, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's again -- that was at the time in August 2001 in any case, Mr. Risto Galevski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, keep the statement in front of you, sir. I'll come back to it. But there is another issue which you've given evidence about it and it's the fact that in your knowledge Mr. Boskoski signed a number of orders of appointment of members of the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that is information that I was -- I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you understand your -- in your answer you are suggesting that you haven't seen any such orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it is your understanding that the practice for Ministers of Interior in Macedonia to sign orders of appointment preceded the time of Mr. Boskoski and continued after his time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to show you another paragraph of Mr. Zafirovski's statement, and it's paragraph 8. It would be the second page, sir, of that statement. And Mr. Zafirovski says the following: "The Minister of Interior was and still is the person that signs the decision for assigning of higher ranked police administrative. That was and still is the case, because the ministry is one legal entity led by the minister. He had and still has that right according to the law. In my experience, it was generally done in accordance to the suggestions of the higher ranks in the ministry, because the minister as a politician generally is not in a position to know the person who are assigned at different positions in the professional hierarchy." So Mr. Zafirovski in effect agrees with you that Mr. Boskoski had the power to make or to sign the decisions for assignment of higher ranking police administrative, which is consistent with what you said?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I hope you will agree also with what Mr. Zafirovski explained from his own experience and expertise which is that the selection or the decision as to who should or could be appointed was made at a lower level, and the decision would then be signed by the minister; is that correct? Or is that a matter that is within your knowledge, I should ask you that you to be fair.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would use the same word as Mr. Zafirovski and say generally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that a matter which is within your knowledge? Would you be privy to situations where either Mr. Boskoski would have personally selected individuals to start with that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no direct knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, or could you confirm in any case, that many of the most senior members of the Ministry of Interior at the time had been appointed not by Mr. Boskoski but by his predecessor?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine before Mr. Boskoski took up his post, the appointments were made by others, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that the first man of the police, Mr. Goran Mitevski was actually pointed by the previous government, not the government of which Mr. Boskoski was a member? Are you knowledgeable of that fact?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was probably aware of that, but I don't recall it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that the first man of the police is appointed not by the Minister of Interior but by the government itself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you also aware of the fact that the first man of the police Mr. Zivko Petrovski was also appointed not by Mr. Boskoski but by his predecessor?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not aware of that. I don't know who appointed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that Mr. Galevski, the first man of the uniformed police, had been pointed not by Mr. Boskoski but his predecessor again?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated in your statement as well that in your experience again, and we're obviously only talking about that here, you witness let's say some reluctance to make decision within the chain of command. Would that be a fair description?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, I think you've indicated that in your experience or in your presence in any case people would often direct you to other persons?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is correct, yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you one other paragraph of Mr. Zafirovski's statement where he described in quite some terms the way in which the police functions in relation to operative decisions and it's at paragraph 6, if you can turn to that. It says this: "On everyday basis, there are hundreds if not thousands operative decisions made at all level of the hierarchy." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "For example, the following decision are done at the lowest level of the hierarchy. The way and the tactics of acting in a specific situation, who are the persons who will be identified and registered, who are the persons who will be searched, which vehicles will be controlled," et cetera. First is that consistent with your, let's say experience with the contacts you had with the police?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely, no. For example it refers to traffic control, vehicles will be controlled, et cetera. Now that is a low-level operational task and that is conducted at a lower level. However, the framework within which individual police officers may operate would be often directed from above, or if there was a low level -- if we say tactical operational response that's required then -- that was unusual, out of the ordinary, then this would be something that they would not feel confident to respond to, often, without further reference from their chain of command. And if I could add, that this is, as I believe, a matter of record from the various agencies of the European -- of the international community and is one of the reasons that the European agency for reconstruction has been providing assistance to the Ministry of Interior and the government in Macedonia to reform.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the reforms, sir, was to decentralise the police further; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: To provide decision making at a lower level yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you talk about referring up your chain of command, would it be correct to say that the sort the matters which you have just identified would generally be dealt with within the police station, generally by the commander of the police station himself?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The items that are listed -- the activities listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The ones that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unusual --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- incidents? It depends on what they are. And once if we observed a reluctance in the field on the part of employees of the Ministry of Interior to respond, or if we were asking them to respond to something, then we were able to observe their end of the communication but were not in a position to observe the communication beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "Furthermore, the following operative decisions are made on a daily basis by the commanders of the police stations: the composition and the strength of the police patrols, the number of engaged employees, the type of weapons, the type of communication means, matters regarding use of vehicles, et cetera, while the following operative measures are created on a medium level in the hierarchy. The way in the system that the police will work according to which significant direction will be controlled on a higher level, which protection means will be used by the police, operative planning, activities of the police for acting on specific problem," and so on. Is that consistent with what you just explained, Mr. Bolton?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Just give me a moment to read through it again, if you would. I don't -- I don't think this reads particularly well. But if I understand it correctly, what Mr. Zafirovski is saying is that the higher level -- there were certain activities that would require higher level input, and that includes -- protection means and operative planning activities. Is -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I have to agree with you that the translation perhaps is not the best. But this is what it seems to say. And would you agree that it's consistent, for example, with what you explained earlier with your contacts with Mr. Bliznakovski?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that these check-points formed part of an operational planning activity and therefore would be at a higher level, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would now ask you to turn to paragraph 7 of the same statement which is on the second page of the statement. Mr. Zafirovski says this: "In my experience and in accordance to the law, the operative measures are not under the authority of the minister because he is not the police administrative but the politics figure. The operative activities were, are, and will be under the authority of the professional police structure. Every attempt to suggest that the Ministry of Interior would come to a decision for the leaving of a check-point is not probable and is opposite to every police logic. For me, as a police administrative who has been effectively working for 27 years in the police, it is unthinkable and absolutely unacceptable." Again, sir, I'm not meaning to criticise you or to do that otherwise, but you would agree that the evidence of Mr. Zafirovski differs quite significantly from yours in relation to the matter of check-points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It differs, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is another matter discussed in your statement and that is the issue of the reporting system within the Ministry of Interior, and I think it would be fair to say that you have been relatively critical of the way in which the reporting system functions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your remarks were essentially to the effect that perhaps the reporting system within the Ministry of Interior was not done as well or as a professionally as one would hope would be the case. Would it be fair?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you also pointed out that the safekeeping of records was again perhaps not as well done as it could or should have been; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And but you also aware that sometimes reporting within the chain of command would be done orally rather than in writing in reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes, and my observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree, I hope, that the fact that the country was in the middle of a crisis may not have contributed to improving the way in which the reporting functioned in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree. I would imagine that that would provide a higher incentive to ensure that reporting is both effective and rapid.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would also increase the incentive perhaps to report orally because of the number of incidents; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a certain level and for practical reasons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd also like to ask you a few questions, if I may, about the way in which the documents were being archived within the OSCE. Could you explain, for example, the documents that we've seen of the 15th of August would be prepared by you and then sent on to, in this case Ambassador Ungaro and a number of other people. Who would be responsible then to archive those documents?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I don't know. I know there was an archive system within the mission headquarters, but I do not know who was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be correct that one copy of your report would be kept in Skopje and another one would usually be sent to the headquarter in Vienna? Would it be correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be correct. My understanding of that procedure, which I have never been directly involved in myself and therefore I may be mistaken, but my understanding of that system is that if the document is transmitted on to Vienna, yes, it is archived in both locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as I understand the access to the OSCE archives would be limited to OSCE personnel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine so. Again, I'm not directly aware of that -- that procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have a strange proposition to put to you and I'm sure you're going to be able to answer it reasonably. If it were to be the case that documents went missing from the archives of the OSCE, you would not infer from that fact that someone would have either done that in intentionally or that was something suspicious about it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- that is essentially correct. If people do not apply the procedures and the practice that is accepted within the OSCE field operations, then, of course, a document may go missing, may turn up somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if of all the daily log sheet, which as the name suggests, the OSCE keeps daily in Macedonia, the only two missing were the ones for the 13th and 14th of August, and again you would agree that you would not necessarily conclude that someone has been involved in a criminal enterprise to hide those documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would want to satisfy myself that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if of all the daily reports from OSCE Radisani, which was your office, were missing for the period 9 to 24th of August, 2001, had disappeared, would you conclude from this that someone in this office or someone in the archives was involved in a criminal enterprise to hide those documents?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be insufficient to conclude that, but I would want to find out -- I would want to investigate internally as to what the reason was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I would just ask to you look at two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If it is possible for the registry to put both documents next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, they are in under tab 71 and 72 in your binder. And for the registry's benefit, they are 1D160, 1D001720, that's tab 71; and 1D161, 1D001721. As you can see, sir, the first letter is a letter by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski to the OSCE in Skopje to the attention of Mr. Victor Ullum, the head of the rule of law section. And it refers to a telephone conversation, and then the letter ask the OSCE to confirm what has been discussed, namely that a number of documents are missing, in particular, daily bulletin or daily log shoot for 13 and 14 of August. The absence of records pertaining to 13 and 14 of August, and the absence of all spillover daily reports from the Radisani team from the period 9 to 24th August. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HENRY BOLTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look on your right on the screen, or tab 72 if you prefer, you will have and you will find the response to that letter by Skopje, OSCE in Skopje, signed by Mr. Ullum and dated 12 February 2007, and it says that as stated on the phone to Mr. Mettraux on 9 February 2007 I personally reviewed the archives of the OSCE spillover monitor mission to Skopje looking for a daily log sheet or daily bulletin bearing the date 13 and 14 of August 2001. I was unable able to find any such document, despite the fact that bulletins both of previous and subsequent date are present in the mission archives. Furthermore, subsequent to your specific request, I searched for and failed to discover any daily reports from the OSCE SMMS, Radisani team, team centre for the period 9 to 24 August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
